0.long_answer: Chromosome 7 spans about 159 million base pairs and constitutes more than 5% of the total DNA in human cells. It has been identified as one of the chromosomes involved in cases of uniparental disomy, where both copies of a chromosome are inherited from one parent, deviating from the typical biparental inheritance pattern. This observation is notable because uniparental disomy can have significant genetic implications including homozygosity for certain alleles, potentially leading to disorders such as neurodevelopmental disorders.
